pr_title: Fixed bug in TopologyManager with SingleNUMANode Policy
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
> Uncomment only one ` /kind <>` line, hit enter to put that in a new line, and remove leading whitespaces from that line:
>
> /kind api-change

/kind bug

> /kind cleanup
> /kind design
> /kind documentation
> /kind failing-test
> /kind feature
> /kind flake

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
This patch fixes an issue where best-effort pods were not admitted
to the node if the single-numa-node policy was set.

This was because the Admit policy in single-numa-node policy does
not admit any pod where the hint is anything but single NUMA node. The 'best hint' in this case is {<set bits for num. Numa Nodes on machine>, true}
So on a machine with 2 NUMA nodes the best hint for a best-effort pod is {11,true} as best-effort pods have no Topology preferences.

The single-numa-node policy fails any pod with a not preferred hint OR a hint where > 1 bits are set, thus the above example resulting in termintaed pods with a Topology Affinity Error.

This is a short term fix for the single-numa-node policy, as there will be code refactoring for the 1.17 release.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

issue_context.title: Pods  error out with 'Topology Affinity Error' if resources and limits are not mentioned as part of the pod spec. This is after #83492
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:

With the latest fix #83697 , which aims to resolve the issue of deploying pods with single-numa-node policy, it seems to have resulted in failure to deploy pods if the pod spec does not have resources and limits constraints. This is resulting in Kube-dns and other pods which do not have resource constraints mentioned fail to deploy due to Topology Affinity Error.
kube-system   kube-dns-b54d5f547-22dks   0/3     Topology Affinity Error   0    


**What you expected to happen**:
Ideally, if there are no resource constraints mentioned we will still need the pod to be deployed. 
We cannot have Kube-dns failing to deploy due to Topology Affinity issue.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
With the latest fix, enabling single-numa-node policy, Kube-dns errors out on the node. 
One can just try to deploy simple pod without resource constraints in pod spec. 

**Anything else we need to know?**:
This happens only when policy is single-numa-node. Pods do not fail to deploy for best-case policy. 

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"16", GitVersion:"v1.16.1", GitCommit:"d647ddbd755faf07169599a625faf302ffc34458", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2019-10-02T17:01:15Z", GoVersion:"go1.12.10", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"17+", GitVersion:"v1.17.0-alpha.1.338+017842d49deca6-dirty", GitCommit:"017842d49deca68dab3a26b76d5dfd5df15a8113", GitTreeState:"dirty", BuildDate:"2019-10-11T10:39:19Z", GoVersion:"go1.12.10", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}

- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: 
   Baremetal x86 server with 2 NUMA nodes and 32 cpus.
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): Fedora 28
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 5.0.13-100.fc28.x86_64

@Deepthidharwar thanks for alerting us to the issue. Can you try the PR linked?

My guess is that this issue was introduced after https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/83492 landed.

Before that, best-effort pods weren't even being considered by the TopologyManager, and the logic for admitting vs. not admitting was skipped.

Which means that we need this fix for this on master, but do not need it on the 1.16 branch.

@zvonkok can you verify if it works as expected in the release-1.16 branch. This would verify my claim that it broke with the introduction of #83492 not the fix from #83697. 

The patch for #83492 landed just a few hours after #83697, so I could see how its hard to know which one caused the new issue.

@klueska , That's right. This fix is needed for the master branch and not 1.16.
 1.16 works well without #83492.

/cc @ConnorDoyle for visibility.

This issue appeared as a result of #83492
Thanks for the ping. So is the proposed fix to always admit best-effort pods in the topology manager?

This only affects the single-numa-node policy because of the "hack" we currently have in place for it: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/cm/topologymanager/topology_manager.go#L248

The right long term fix is to address this as part of: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/83478

However, if we want to put a short term fix in place to "unbreak" master, @lmdaly has a PR linked above that will fix the immediate problem.

review_comments:
I see how this would fix the issue because of the one-off hack we currently have in the `TopologyManager`, i.e. where we intercept hints that have more than one NUMA affinity and force them to `false`.

However, since this is only broken on master, I'm inclined to wait for a proper fix in the form of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/83478.

What do others think?
